record.what_it_does: API for parsing, extracting, splitting, classifying and editing documents into structured data.
record.auth_notes: A static API key sent as Authorization: Bearer $REDUCTO_API_KEY. You create keys in Studio (studio.reducto.ai/api-keys) or inline on the quickstart page after signing in. There is no OAuth, so each user would supply their own key. The record now lists one auth method (api_key) because the Bearer header is just how the key is sent.
record.access_notes: The quickstart says "Sign up for a free account" and you can then create a key right away. The Standard plan is pay-as-you-go and includes $150 in free usage. Growth and Enterprise plans go through sales.
record.api_breadth_notes: About 20 operations. Parse, Extract, Split, Classify, Edit and Pipeline each have sync and async versions. Upload and delete upload. Jobs: get, list, cancel, delete. Configure webhook, and Version. These are document-processing functions, not CRUD resources.
record.mcp_notes: Reducto hosts it at https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp and documents it at docs.reducto.ai/mcp-server. Auth is the API key as Authorization: Bearer. I opened the page directly and confirmed these details.
record.blocker_notes: The API is public, self-serve and comes with $150 of free credit. Auth uses a user-supplied API key rather than OAuth. The API is narrow in purpose (document processing) but has a reasonable number of operations.
